quarterly_data.signal: SolarEdge's 10-K: fiscal 2025 revenues were $1,184,444 thousand, up 31.4% from $901,456 thousand in 2024 (United States $718,227 thousand, Europe $317,595 thousand, international markets $148,622 thousand); gross profit was $196,281 thousand (16.6% of revenue) versus a gross loss of 97.3% in 2024; net loss was $405.4 million versus $1,806.4 million. The company says 2025 sales increased due to more normalized channel inventory in both the United States and Europe despite prolonged softness in demand.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenues $1,184,444 thousand (+31.4%); gross profit $196,281 thousand (16.6%); net loss $405.4 million

quarterly_data.signal: SolarEdge's 10-K revenue by product line for fiscal 2025: optimizers $489.9M (+55.6% YoY vs $314.9M), inverters $333.8M (+34.8% vs $247.6M), batteries $285.4M (+49.8% vs $190.5M), energy storage systems $16.4M (-67.1% vs $49.9M). Units recognized as revenue in 2025: 349.6 thousand inverters (245.7 thousand in 2024), 10,571.4 thousand power optimizers (6,645.8 thousand) and 897.4 MWh of batteries (556.2 MWh). Because of its Single SKU concept the company no longer reports Megawatts shipped, starting with the fourth quarter of 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: optimizers $489.9M (+55.6%); inverters $333.8M (+34.8%); batteries $285.4M (+49.8%); 349.6 thousand inverters, 10,571.4 thousand optimizers, 897.4 MWh batteries

quarterly_data.signal: SolarEdge's 10-K customer concentration: Consolidated Electrical Distributors, Inc represented 18.6% of 2025 revenues and no other customer exceeded ten percent; the top three customers together represented 35.8% of 2025 revenues (one major customer was 12.9% in 2024; two were 24.0% in 2023). Customers are mainly solar distributors, electrical equipment wholesalers and large installers. In November 2025 customer Posigen, Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, leading to cancellations of orders.
quarterly_data.figure: Consolidated Electrical Distributors 18.6% of 2025 revenues; top three customers 35.8%

quarterly_data.signal: SolarEdge's 10-K manufacturing and suppliers: its solar products are made by two contract manufacturers, Jabil Inc. and Flex Ltd., which together accounted for 50.7% of trade payables at December 31, 2025 (43.4% a year earlier). The vast majority of products are now made in the United States - inverters in Texas, optimizers and inverters in Florida, batteries in Utah - after manufacturing in China, Mexico and Hungary was discontinued; a minor portion is made at its own Sella 1 facility in Israel and some capability is kept in Vietnam with a third-party manufacturer. It depends on limited or single source suppliers for certain key components and raw materials, some subcomponents are still imported from China, and it is exploring alternative suppliers outside China.
quarterly_data.figure: two contract manufacturers 50.7% of trade payables (December 31, 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: SolarEdge's 10-K commitments: purchase obligations of $513.2 million related to raw materials and commitments for the future manufacturing of its products (a provision for loss of $24,324 thousand recorded against them) and open capital expenditure commitments of approximately $23.5 million for automated assembly lines and other manufacturing machinery, as of December 31, 2025. Deferred revenues and customer advances (remaining performance obligations) totaled $363,699 thousand, of which $70,371 thousand is expected in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: purchase obligations $513.2 million; capex commitments approximately $23.5 million; deferred revenues $363,699 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: SolarEdge's 10-K product roadmap: the next-generation SolarEdge Nexis inverters are in the process of being launched - the Nexis Inverter 3ph designed to provide between 8-20 kW for the three-phase residential market and the Nexis Inverter 1ph designed to provide 3.8-13 kW for the single-phase residential market.
